Who are we

At Restored Rarity, restoration goes far beyond surface cleaning. It is a careful, detail-driven process designed to bring each card as close as possible to its original appearance while preserving the character and history that make it unique.

From deep creases, dents, and pressure marks to edge damage, surface imperfections, warping, delamination, and years of accumulated wear, every card presents a different challenge. That's why there is no one-size-fits-all approach. Each card is individually evaluated, and the restoration process is tailored to its specific condition, construction, and damage.

Some cards respond beautifully in a single session. Others require multiple rounds, specialized techniques, and patience to address years of wear or the card's natural tendency to retain a “memory” of previous damage. Every step is approached carefully and deliberately, with the goal of achieving the best result the card can realistically provide.

Restoration is as much about judgment and patience as it is technique. Knowing how a card responds, when to continue, when to adjust the approach, and when the best possible result has been achieved is an important part of the process.

Whether you're looking to revive a childhood favorite, improve the presentation of a centerpiece in your collection, prepare a card for grading evaluation, or give new life to a card you thought was beyond saving, Restored Rarity is dedicated to the cards worth preserving.

Your collection has a history. Let us preserve it.

Submission FAQ

Read through before submitting or shipping your cards.

How do I submit cards for restoration?

Start by completing the Restored Rarity Submission Form above. You'll provide your contact information, details about each card, its estimated Near Mint value, and the cleaning or restoration service you're interested in.

Submitting the form begins the process, but it does not mean you should ship your cards yet.

What happens after I submit my request?

Once your form has been submitted, you'll receive an automatic confirmation email letting you know your request was successfully received.

From there, I'll personally review your submission and follow up by email. We'll confirm your requested services, discuss any questions about the cards or damage, review shipping details and costs, and provide an estimated restoration timeline.

How does shipping work?

Shipping costs are passed through to the customer and are separate from the cost of your selected services.

During our initial communication, I'll confirm the shipping method, cost, insurance/value information, and other necessary details with you. Once everything is confirmed and I'm ready to receive your submission, I'll provide your shipping label and shipping instructions by email.

Return shipping will also be coordinated with you, with appropriate shipping and insurance based on the value of the cards being returned.

How should I package my cards?

Cards should be packaged carefully to protect against movement, bending, moisture, and impact during transit.

I recommend following the general card-shipping practices outlined by PSA: cards should be individually protected with a penny sleeve and semi-rigid holder such as a Card Saver, kept in the same order as your submission when possible, and secured with appropriate rigid support and cushioning inside a sturdy shipping box.

Avoid packaging that places unnecessary pressure directly on the cards or allows them to move freely inside the package.

Specific packaging and shipping instructions will also be provided before you send your submission.

What happens when my cards arrive?

Once received, your cards will be documented and physically inspected. I'll compare their condition with the information provided on your submission and confirm that the requested services are appropriate for the damage present.

Photos don't always tell the entire story. If the physical inspection reveals additional damage, a different repair level, or something that changes the scope or cost of the restoration, I'll contact you before proceeding.

There are no surprise upgrades or additional repairs performed without communication when they would change what we originally discussed.

How long will my restoration take?

Turnaround time varies with every submission and will be discussed with you during our initial emails before you ship your cards.

Card restoration isn't a one-size-fits-all process. A cleaning or minor repair may be relatively straightforward, while significant creases, dents, lifting, edge damage, or delamination can require multiple rounds of treatment, different techniques, and appropriate drying or stabilization time.

Some damage can also have a natural tendency to retain “memory,” making patience and additional rounds necessary to achieve a more stable result.

The priority is always achieving the best and most stable result the card will realistically allow—not rushing a restoration to meet an arbitrary turnaround time.

If circumstances significantly change the expected timeline while your cards are with me, I'll communicate that with you.

Will you automatically perform additional repairs if you find more damage?

No. If I discover damage that falls outside the service or repair level we originally discussed, I'll contact you first.

I'll explain what I found, what I recommend, and any difference in price before performing additional work that would change your approved service.

How are high-value cards handled?

Value surcharges apply to repair services only — cleaning and evaluation services are never subject to a surcharge, no matter the card's value.

For repairs, cards with a Near Mint value of $500 or less do not have a card-value surcharge.

For repairs on cards valued between $500 and $1,500, a surcharge of 10% of the card's Near Mint value is added to the selected service price. For repairs on cards valued between $1,501 and $2,500, the surcharge rate is 12%. All surcharges are rounded up to the nearest dollar.

Cards valued above $2,500 Near Mint are individually reviewed and require a custom quote.

Are restoration results guaranteed?

No two damaged cards respond exactly the same way, so a specific cosmetic result cannot be guaranteed.

Restoration can significantly improve defects, but evidence of the original damage may sometimes remain. For example, a repaired crease may leave surface scarring, rubs, or changes to the foil appearance even though the crease itself has been corrected.

Damage memory can also occasionally cause a faint indication of previous damage to reappear after a restoration.

This is restoration, not alteration. The goal is to carefully correct what can be corrected while preserving the card and achieving the best result it will realistically allow.

Can you guarantee a specific grading result?

No. Grade-Ready Evaluations are evaluations—not grading guarantees.

I can identify defects, address eligible issues, clean and prepare the card, and provide my assessment of its grading potential. However, PSA, TAG, CGC, BGS, or any other third-party grading company independently determines the final grade.

How will I know what's happening with my submission?

Communication is a major part of the Restored Rarity process. The email address provided on your submission form will be the primary method of communication for:

Submission confirmation and initial review, estimated turnaround, shipping labels and instructions, service or repair recommendations, pricing changes requiring approval, restoration updates when necessary, and completion, payment, and return shipping.

Please use an email address you regularly check and keep an eye on your inbox after submitting.

What happens when my restoration is finished?

Once your restoration is complete, I'll contact you with the final details and coordinate getting your cards safely back to you.

Your cards will be securely packaged for their return trip, and return shipping and applicable insurance costs will be passed through to you and confirmed before shipment.

From the moment you submit your request until your cards make their way home, the goal is simple: clear communication, careful handling, and no surprises.

TERMS & CONDITIONS

Effective Date: September 9, 2026

Please read carefully before submitting your request.

By checking the acknowledgment box and submitting a service request to Restored Rarity, you confirm that you have read, understand, and agree to these Terms & Conditions and Waiver of Liability.

1. Authorization to Perform Services

By submitting cards to Restored Rarity, you represent that you are the lawful owner of the cards or are otherwise authorized by the owner to request services.

You authorize Restored Rarity to perform the cleaning, evaluation, repair, and/or restoration services that you approve for your submission.

Depending on the selected service and condition of the card, services may include cleaning, surface refinement, scratch buffing, crease reduction, dent or gouge repair, corner or edge repair, flattening, delamination repair, and other restoration techniques reasonably necessary to perform the approved service.

2. Inherent Risks of Card Restoration

Trading cards are delicate, layered collectibles. Cleaning, repairing, or restoring an already damaged card involves inherent risk.

Even when reasonable care is exercised, restoration may result in unintended changes to a card's surface, foil, gloss, texture, printing, color, edges, corners, layers, adhesives, or other materials.

Pre-existing, underlying, or previously hidden damage may also become more apparent during or after restoration.

Some changes may be an unavoidable consequence of attempting to correct existing damage and do not necessarily indicate that a restoration was improperly performed.

By authorizing services, you acknowledge and accept the inherent risks reasonably associated with the approved cleaning, repair, or restoration procedures.

Nothing in these Terms is intended to waive or limit liability that cannot legally be waived or limited under applicable law.

3. Restoration, Not Alteration

The objective of Restored Rarity is to restore, repair, and preserve the original card while achieving the best result the card will realistically allow.

Restoration does not mean manufacturing a perfect card, and Restored Rarity cannot guarantee that all evidence of previous damage will disappear.

A repaired crease, for example, may still leave surface scarring, foil disruption, rubs, texture changes, or other visible evidence of the original damage even when the underlying crease has been substantially improved.

4. Damage Memory & Long-Term Results

Trading cards are composed of layered materials that may retain what Restored Rarity refers to as “damage memory.”

In some cases, a crease, indentation, warp, lift, or other previously repaired defect may partially or faintly reappear days, weeks, or months after restoration.

This may occur due to the severity of the original damage, card construction, manufacturing processes, adhesive quality, environmental conditions, storage conditions, temperature, humidity, or other factors.

The reappearance of a defect does not necessarily indicate that the restoration was improperly performed.

If an eligible repaired defect resurfaces, contact Restored Rarity so the card can be evaluated. When appropriate, an additional round of eligible repair may be performed at no additional service charge.

The customer remains responsible for applicable shipping costs unless otherwise agreed.

5. No Guarantee of Restoration Results

Specific restoration results are not guaranteed.

Every card, print run, material, and type of damage may respond differently to restoration. Photographs and customer descriptions may also fail to reveal the full extent of a card's condition.

Restored Rarity will use reasonable care and judgment in performing approved services, but complete removal or correction of any defect cannot be guaranteed.

Some cards may require multiple rounds, different techniques, or extended drying and stabilization periods to achieve the best result realistically possible.

6. Grading & No Guarantee of Grade

Cleaning, restoration, repair, grading preparation, or a Grade-Ready Evaluation does not guarantee any particular grade or grading outcome.

Any grade estimate or evaluation provided by Restored Rarity represents an opinion based on the observable condition of the card at the time of evaluation.

Final grading, authentication, designation, and acceptance decisions are made solely by the applicable third-party grading company.

Restored Rarity is not responsible if a card receives a grade lower than anticipated, does not receive a numerical grade, is rejected or declined, or receives an altered, restored, authentic-only, or similar designation.

You acknowledge that cleaning, repair, or restoration may affect how a third-party grading company evaluates, authenticates, labels, or grades a card.

Unless expressly stated otherwise, Restored Rarity is not affiliated with PSA, TAG, CGC, BGS, or any other third-party grading company.

7. Card Value Surcharge

Card-value surcharges apply to repair services only. Cleaning and evaluation services are never subject to a value surcharge, regardless of the card's Near Mint value.

For repair services, cards valued at $500 or less in Near Mint condition are not subject to a card-value surcharge.

For repair services on cards valued above $500, an additional surcharge is added to the selected service price based on the card's current Near Mint TCG market value.

It does not establish or represent an agreed replacement value, guaranteed resale value, guaranteed post-restoration value, or amount payable in the event of loss or damage.

The Near Mint value used for service pricing may differ substantially from the current value of a damaged card.

Restored Rarity reserves the right to individually review higher-value cards before accepting them for service.

Additional documentation or precautions may be required before a high-value card is accepted, including photographs, proof of value, specialized packaging, signature-required shipping, or other reasonable security measures.

Restored Rarity reserves the right to decline any card or submission based on card value, condition, restoration risk, shipping considerations, or other reasonable business considerations.

After submitting a request, the customer will receive confirmation that the submission has been received. Restored Rarity will then review the submission and contact the customer directly by email.

DO NOT SHIP CARDS UNTIL RESTORED RARITY HAS CONTACTED YOU AND SPECIFICALLY AUTHORIZED YOU TO DO SO.
